answer: Before an agent can bid, it must buy a one-time quartz serial from the kernel registrar and publish a receipt bound to its address for three epochs. Peers attest only when that serial is live and unique; a reused or shared serial is slashed on the spot. Identities may wander under new names, but a spent serial cannot move with them, so a farm of 800 aliases must buy 800 distinct quartz serials and risks losing every linked receipt if any two collide.
